blocks.html: Despite widening after the war, credit spreads continue to be very tight from a historical perspective. Investment Grade (IG) spreads entered Q1 at roughly 78 basis points — just above 20- year lows. By March 31st, IG spreads had widened to approximately 89 basis points, putting current spreads in the 13th percentile on a 20- year lookback. The story in high yield was very similar in character. HY spreads entered the year at ~ 266 basis points and finished the quarter in the 300– 345 basis point range. With the 20- year average for HY at ~ 488 basis points, even after the Q1 widening, spreads in both markets remain well below long-term averages and inside historical stress levels. Neither market is signaling systemic credit stress; the widening observed is consistent with a measured, geopolitical risk repricing rather than any deterioration in underlying corporate fundamentals.

blocks.html: Private credit is illiquid by nature. Promising regular redemptions does not change the fundamental liquidity dynamics of the underlying instruments. What this means, practically speaking, is that the retail system depends on continued inflows to function properly. And therein lies the crux of the problem we are watching play out in real time. As we discussed in our recent note “Not All Private Credit Is The Same,” private credit BDCs have an inherent asset-liability mismatch. blocks.html: In December 2025, BP PMKN LLC (“BP PMKN”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of BasePoint Capital III LLC, provided interim bridge financing (the “Bridge Financing”) to its wholly owned acquisition vehicle, IPF Parent Holdings Limited (“UK Bidco”) for the pending acquisition of IPF. Under the UK Takeover Code, a bidder must demonstrate that it has suﬃcient financial resources to implement the oﬀer by the time a firm intention to make an oﬀer is announced. This UK process of a deal’s “cash confirmation” is typically satisfied through committed financing arrangements from banks or other institutions or by having funds readily available (for example, cash on hand or placed in escrow). To satisfy these requirements, BP PMKN funded an escrow account on behalf of UK Bidco in the amount of $549,602,200 to satisfy “cash confirmation” requirements. The funding was documented through two instruments (i) a $274,801,100 USD-denominated note issued by UK Bidco (the “Eurobond”) and (ii) a $274,801,100 secured promissory note issued by BP PMKN. BasePoint expects to refinance the Bridge Financing in full at or shortly prior to the closing of the acquisition. The Fund will have the option, but will not be obligated, to participate in the permanent financing of the acquisition. If the acquisition does not close, the funds in the escrow account will be released from the escrow account and returned to BP PMKN.

blocks.html: Landing, founded in 2019 and headquartered in Birmingham, AL, offers fully furnished, flexible-lease apartments through a nationwide network spanning more than 250 cities. In 2025 the Company wound down its Standard Program and fully transitioned to its Autopilot Program. Under the Autopilot Program, Landing enters into longer-term agreements, typically up to five years, with building owners to provide immediate lease-up occupancy in exchange for a revenue split. In March 2024, Landing completed an acquisition of the assets of Barsala, a platform that offers flexible, quick lease-up options to multi-family buildings owners and offers furnished, flexible term leases to customers through its website.
